name: Sadid al-Din al-Bahnasi
bio: Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Hasan al-Muhallabi al-Bahnasi came from al-Bahnasa in Upper Egypt; the manuscripts of his commentary on Qutrub's triplets call him Sadid al-Din Abu al-Qasim, and al-Zirikli identifies him with the judge Wajih al-Din al-Bahnasi. He began as a copyist and became a leading Shafi'i jurist, learned in legal theory, grammar and letters; made judge of Egypt and Cairo in 680 AH (1281 CE), he lost Cairo and the Delta a year later and kept Fustat and Upper Egypt until he died. He put Qutrub's triplets into verse and wrote his own commentary on the poem, which spread so widely that it was taken for Qutrub's. Al-Subki tells of a student who complained of his lot and kept saying “four” with the wrong ending, until the judge asked him, “Scholar, who made your fours indeclinable?” He died in 685 AH (1286 CE), the year al-Asnawi and Ibn Qadi Shuhba give.
